notes: 111 first-pass sentences. NG91: public info and evidence summary confirm no antibiotic or back-up for most, immediate antibiotics when very unwell/serious illness/high risk, and 'might also' for fluid from ear or under 2 with both ears; the first-pass reassessment/resistant-organisms sentence was not retrieved and was removed. Glue ear: 'under 7', 'plastic tubes', 'fluid stays for weeks' and the 'NHS leaflet' attribution were not supported; reworded to hospital leaflets (Alder Hey, Dorset, Imperial) and 'one UK parent guide'; glue-ear details come from hospital leaflets, not nhs.uk/conditions/glue-ear itself. Smoke: 'major cause' not retrieved; CDC says children whose parents smoke get more ear infections and advises avoiding secondhand smoke. Care routes: the NHS England page (as summarised) does not list 999 or a 'same day GP/111' route for swelling behind the ear, headache or facial twitching; the latter now attributed to MedlinePlus (US) and the former to one NHS trust page (Rotherham) plus a generic 'In an emergency, call 999' signposting line (textbook). NHS urgent list: two search summaries agree on generally unwell, very high temperature, swelling around ear, new hearing loss, dizzy/being sick and under-12-months both ears; fluid coming out of the ear also appeared in two summaries but nhs.uk was only seen via summaries. NHS Wales/Rotherham use under 2 for the bilateral threshold; NHS England says under 12 months. Article block is about 1270 words, slightly above the 1200 target. Search tool returned summaries not page text, so some attributions to a single URL are by title only.
